messages.author: d5395aefa96f73b1
messages.subject: reduce combine problem
parts:
Hi All

I'm parsing a text file which contains the folowing lines:

01:47:20 48 172.23.113.156 /NOTIFY SYSTEM SYSTEM GET 200 443 363 null
null null
01:47:30 15 172.23.113.156 /NOTIFY SYSTEM SYSTEM GET 200 443 363 null
null null
01:47:30 10 172.23.113.156 /NOTIFY SYSTEM SYSTEM GET 200 297 363 null
null null
23:20:08 41 172.23.113.156 /NOTIFY SYSTEM SYSTEM GET 200 389 363 null
null null
23:20:15 16 172.23.113.156 /NOTIFY SYSTEM SYSTEM GET 200 436 363 null
null null

The map pase works fine but after trying various techniques during the
reduce phase i'm still
not able to save averages, max's, min's, etc to a text file. I seem to
keep on hitting my head against
the combine for the final rhcollect(). Any assistance would be
apreciated. Below are a few examples with their results:

rhcollect(reduce.key, columnSums)
/NOTIFY 5.0 130.0 2008.0 1815.0

rhcollect(reduce.key, columnMeans)
/NOTIFY 1.0 26.0 401.6 363.0

rr <- c(columnSums, columnMeans)
rhcollect(reduce.key, rr)
/NOTIFY 5.0 130.0 2008.0 1815.0 1.0 26.0 401.6 363.0 5.0 130.0 2008.0
1815.0 1.0 26.0 401.6 363.0

rr <- c(1, columnSums, 2)
rhcollect(reduce.key, rr)
/NOTIFY 1.0 1.0 5.0 130.0 2008.0 1815.0 2.0 2.0


R
library(Rhipe)
rhinit(TRUE, TRUE)

map <- expression({
tryCatch({
tkn <- strsplit(unlist(map.values)," ")
rows <- do.call("rbind",tkn)
apply(rows[,c(4,2,9,10)], 1, function(r){
nv <- as.numeric(r[2])
bi <- as.numeric(r[3])
bo <- as.numeric(r[4])
rhcollect(r[1], c(1, nv, bi,bo))
})
},error=function(e){
rhstatus(sprintf("ERROR: Read : %s", e$message))
rhcounter("RERRORS","Wrong Length", 1)
})
})

reduce <- expression(
pre={
results <- NULL
dMatrix <- NULL
finals <- NULL
sums <- NULL
columnSums <- NULL
columnMeans <- NULL
sumsTme <- NULL
avgTme <- NULL
minTme <- NULL
maxTme <- NULL
}
,reduce= {
results <- rbind(results,do.call(rbind, reduce.values))
dMatrix <- as.matrix(results, ncol=4)
finals <- cbind(finals, dMatrix)
}
,post={
columnSums <- colSums(finals)
columnMeans <- colMeans(finals)
sums <- columnSums[1]
sumsTme <- columnSums[2]
avgTme <- columnMeans[2]
rr <- NULL
rr <- c(1, columnSums, 2)
rhcollect(reduce.key, rr)
}
)

z <- rhmr(map=map, reduce=reduce,combine=TRUE, ,ifolder="/logs/
log20110917.log",ofolder="/usr/hduser/rhipe",jobname="RHipe")
rhex(z,async=FALSE)

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Re: reduce combine problem
parts:
Undocumented. And i never thought this would be used.

See the value of '.rhipe.current.state'

In map stage == "map"

in combine == "map.combine"
in reduce == "reduce"


in map.setup, it is "map.setup" and "map.cleanup" durin map cleanup.

If a combiner is used, try and set your map output to be the same shape as the reducer output. This is because
during the mapping stage, the rhcollect sends output to a buffe, when this buffer reaches a mark, the reducer is called (on the map nodes, this is not the Reduce of MapReduce). The output of the reducer is then sorted and sent across the network to the reducers.

Cheers
Saptarshi

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Re: reduce combine problem
parts:
If i understood Piet correctly,

1. conditioned on col(4) (e..g /NOTIFY) compute
 a) mean, max,min for each of columns 2,9 and 10


Then what we can do in one pass with RHIPE is compute

1. conditioned on col(4) (e..g /NOTIFY) compute
 a) **# of obs**, sum, max,min for each of columns 2,9 and 10

(note, not the mean) You'd have to compute the mean in another pass (which shouldn't require RHIPE).

Here's the code - tested on a file. I dont use rhipe.current.state and neither should others - if a key has few rows it might never be called!
Note
1.  the           ,zips    = "/user/sguha/Rfolder.tar.gz" is not rquired, i need it for my cluster (no R on nodes)
2. the file foo.txt can be found here http://people.mozilla.com:~/sguha/foo.txt
  - download it and place in the HDFS

Hope it helps
Saptarshi


map <- expression({
  tryCatch({
    rows <- do.call('rbind',strsplit(unlist(map.values)," +"))
apply(rows[,c(4,2,9,10)], 1, function(r){

nv <- as.numeric(r[2:4])
      for(i in seq_along(nv)){
        rhcollect(list(r[1],col.id=i), list(count=1, sum=nv[i], max=nv[i],min=nv[i]))

}
    })
  },error=function(e){
    rhstatus(sprintf("ERROR: Read : %s", e$message))
rhcounter("R_ERRORS",as.character(e), 1)

})
})

reduce <- expression(
    pre={

counts <- 0 ; sums <- 0; mins <- Inf;maxs <- -Inf;
      getName <- function(lst,nm) unlist(lapply(lst,function(j) j[[nm]]))
    }
    ,reduce={
      counts <- counts + sum(getName(reduce.values,"count") )
      sums   <- sums   + sum(getName(reduce.values,"sum") )
      maxs   <- max( c(maxs,getName(reduce.values,"max")) )
      mins   <- min( c(mins,getName(reduce.values,"min")) )
    }
    ,post={
      ## We have no idea if this the last reduce$post for this key ...
      ## So we cannot output a mean ...
      rhcollect(reduce.key, list(count=counts,sum=sums,max=maxs,min=mins))
    }
    )

z <- rhmr(map=map,reduce=reduce, combine=TRUE
          ,ifolder = "/user/sguha/tmp/foo.txt"
          ,ofolder = "/user/sguha/tmp/tmp.txt"
          ,inout   = c("text","text")
          ,zips    = "/user/sguha/Rfolder.tar.gz"
          ,mapred  = list(mapred.textoutputformat.separator = " ")
          )
rhstatus(rhex(z,async=TRUE),mon.sec=5)
## Final data set has 1 row per /NOTIFY object and COL.ID (id == 1,2,3
## coresponding to 2,9 and 10)
rhread("/user/sguha/tmp/tmp.txt/p*",type='text')
## e.g
##      [,1]                                    
## [1,] "/NOTIFY 1 486.0 12658.0 48.0 10.0\r"   
## [2,] "/NOTIFY 2 486.0 195219.0 443.0 297.0\r"
## [3,] "/NOTIFY 3 486.0 176418.0 363.0 363.0\r"
## [4,] "/FOOFIFY 1 14.0 342.0 48.0 10.0\r"     
## [5,] "/FOOFIFY 2 14.0 5581.0 443.0 297.0\r"  
## [6,] "/FOOFIFY 3 14.0 5082.0 363.0 363.0\r"  


## R version
a=read.table("~/tmp/foo.txt")
do.call('rbind',lapply(split(a,a$V4),function(r){
   N <- "V9"
   c(nrow(r),sum(r[,N]),max(r[,N]),min(r[,N]))
 }))

map <- expression({
  tryCatch({
    rows <- do.call('rbind',strsplit(unlist(map.values)," +"))

rhcollect(list(r[1],col.id=i), c(count=1, sum=nv[i], max=nv[i],min=nv[i]))

}

    rhstatus(sprintf("ERROR: Read : %s", e$message))

  })
})

reduce <- expression(
    pre={
      counts <- 0 ; sums <- 0; mins <- Inf;maxs <- -Inf;

    }

      sums   <- sums   + sum(getName(reduce.values,"sum") )
      maxs   <- max( c(maxs,getName(reduce.values,"max")) )
      mins   <- min( c(mins,getName(reduce.values,"min")) )

parts:
I didn't mention this, but when Saptarshi said, "Have the data come
from the map in the same shape", I realized that was the simple way to
go about this, and wished I could draw that out.


Several days went by and today I found myself having to write a simple
test for the combiner, and I decided to base one of the test on this
use case of extracting summary statistics from an nxp matrix divided
up into m chunks on your HDFS.

I uploaded the script as an example of how to approach this problem
here: https://gist.github.com/2070099


It is adaptable to your problem. The main parts that would need
altering is what happens in the map prior to calling emit.summary.


The use of this combiner is space efficient. Essentially the summary
statistics are recombined at least 4 times. Once per a reduce$reduce
in the combiner, once per a reduce$post in the combiner, once per a
reduce$reduce in the actual reduce, and once per a reduce$post in the
actual reduce. Each time the shape of the data stays the same, so the
same function can be reapplied to the input.
